A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DeLiVR. All 14 pages of v1 and 18 pages of v2, including figures, tables, equations and appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original restoration results, component ablations, efficiency measurements and downstream visual evaluations in Section 4 and Tables 1–3.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds optical-flow comparisons, rotation-perturbation analysis and qualitative restoration and detection experiments.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same rotation prediction, spatial and temporal biases, attention integration and training objective. The new flow-bias comparator and additional restoration tasks do not establish a change to DeLiVR itself.

E1.justification: The four original deraining benchmarks remain. Appendix A.3 adds deblurring and dehazing experiments, identifying GoPro and RESIDE as training datasets. Section 4.3 adds synthetic rotation perturbations, and Appendix A.4 extends downstream detection to a real captured rainy image.

E2.justification: v2 adds direct optical-flow comparisons: a RAFT-to-MLP attention-bias baseline on NTURain, plus Yang et al. (2019)'s frame-consistent recurrent model and Fang and Zhan (2022)'s optical-flow/frame-recurrent model on WeatherBench. The original comparator sets in Tables 1 and 3 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 introduces controlled evaluation designs: injecting small rotations into selected frames, and comparing bias representations while holding a 12-layer Transformer and training protocol fixed. Attention maps and distributions provide additional diagnostic measurements. The original benchmark metrics and optimization schedule remain unchanged; omitted AMP/crop descriptions do not establish altered training.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component ablations, v2 adds rotation-perturbation and attention analyses testing alignment behavior, a controlled flow-versus-Lie-bias comparison, and a real-world detection case study. Figures 5 and 8–10 supply new diagnostic evidence. Figure 4's existing visual ablation is retained with a corrected caption.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or comparable uncertainty estimates. The new attention-weight and entropy distributions describe model activations, rather than uncertainty in experimental performance.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain all numerical values. New results include a reported 2.43 dB NTURain advantage over the controlled flow-bias baseline, and WeatherBench PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS of 23.33/0.691/0.455 for Yang et al. (2019) and 24.10/0.716/0.402 for Fang and Zhan (2022). Figures 5 and 7–10 add attention, restoration and detection outcomes; these are additional results, not improved scores for the retained experiments.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and Appendix A.1 retain the same SO(2) definitions, rotation-validity argument, tangent-space discussion and logarithmic displacement reasoning. No new theorem, proof or substantive mathematical correction is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract's scientific claims, introduction contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same novelty, alignment, deraining and downstream-benefit claims. Additional experiments support the existing headline contributions without redefining them.

C2.justification: New passages interpret attention behavior and controlled comparisons as evidence of stronger alignment, and Appendix A.3 describes the prior as degradation-agnostic. Section 4.2.1 removes the incorrect interpretation that VDMamba's lower LPIPS indicates poorer perceptual quality. Existing limitations concerning rotation-only modeling and computational overhead remain.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a public-code repository link and documents the new comparison's 12-layer backbone, RAFT-to-MLP construction and A100 evaluation hardware. However, Section 4.1 removes v1's explicit AMP and 256×256 random-crop details. These are documentation changes; repository contents and changes to the original training procedure are not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: Four references are added: Yang et al. (2019) and Fang and Zhan (2022) for flow-based comparisons, and Nah et al. (2017) and Li et al. (2019) for the additional restoration datasets. Section 2 and the principal novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording edits, removes the experimental roadmap, inserts experimental and appendix subsections, and updates affiliations, equal-contribution information and publication headers. The main narrative, method exposition and section order are largely retained.

P2.justification: Visual material expands substantially through the attention dashboard and new restoration, detection and flow-comparison panels in Figures 5 and 7–10. Figure 11 enlarges existing Figure 3; the original downstream Figure 5 becomes Figure 6. Figure 4 is relocated and its incorrect caption repaired, with accompanying figure/table reflow.

improvement.justification: The controlled flow comparison and rotation-perturbation analysis provide more direct support for the alignment rationale than v1 offered. Additional qualitative applications, the code-access disclosure and corrected Figure 4 caption also help. The gains remain limited by incompletely specified new protocols and predominantly qualitative support for broader applicability, while removing AMP/crop details weakens reproducibility documentation. Overall, the evidence supports a modest net improvement.
